Completing a run with a SKIPPED stop strands its orders on the happy path, exactly as cancelling does
symptom: updateRunStatus's COMPLETED gate treats SKIPPED as done (routes.service.ts:1424 filters s.status !== COMPLETED && s.status !== SKIPPED), so a run with a skipped stop completes normally and that stop's orders keep routeRunStopId against a finished run — the same permanent PREVIOUSLY_DISPATCHED strand as B129, but reached with no cancel involved. B129 as filed covers only the CANCELLED branch. F11's B34/B146 make driver-initiated skips reachable for the first time, so this batch INCREASES the frequency of an uncovered strand. Found by the F11 batch synthesis, 2026-09-02.

title: A SKIPPED stop has no reopen or skip control anywhere in the product — a dead-end state, not just a strand
location: apps/mobile/app/(operator)/route-runs/[id].tsx — stop row actions (:461-468); no web stop-reopen caller exists
symptom: reopenStop (routes.service.ts ~:2695-2697) accepts a SKIPPED stop and would flip a COMPLETED run back to IN_PROGRESS, but POST /route-runs/:id/stops/:stopId/reopen has exactly one client repo-wide — useReopenStop (apps/mobile/lib/api/routes.ts ~:674-683) — whose only caller renders the control solely for s.status === COMPLETED; a SKIPPED stop falls to the null branch, and apps/web has no stop-reopen caller at all. So B211's stranded orders have no in-product recovery and B146's 'only until a human intervenes' was false. Found by the F11 analysis (Opus A, 2026-09-02). Batch is an OWNER call: the file is co-touched by F11 (B129's cancel button :385+) and F20 (B32 :351/:379) — filed unbatched so it lands in triage.

title: A same-key retry after a failed idempotency-key write re-folds an already-committed buyer merge
symptom: After a committed buyer merge, a failed recordIdempotencyKey call is only logged (orders.controller.ts:207-213), so a client retry with the same idempotency key re-runs the fold and computes ABSOLUTE totals a second time over the same cart -- the same swallowed-money-failure class as B58 (F18 sibling-sweep finding, 2026-09-06). A complete fix collides with the standing rule that customer merges serialize through withAdvisoryLock with no transaction threaded into updateOrderItems; recorded in F18's result.json as a deferred owner question (is the accepted failure still acceptable, should recordIdempotencyKey move inside the merge transaction, or should the merge fail closed when the record cannot be written), not fixed by F18.

title: Reinstating a lapsed tenant does not clear a downgrade armed before the lapse
symptom: F18 made onSubscriptionDeleted/onSubscriptionUpdated clear downgradeToPlanKey/downgradeEffectiveAt/retainedUserIds, matching the one-armed-transition invariant subscription-mutation.service.ts now documents, but onPaymentSucceeded and onCheckoutCompleted (the reinstatement webhooks) do not: a tenant that lapses with a downgrade already armed keeps that stale schedule through reinstatement, so the next 02:00 sweep re-prices basePriceSnapshot against the pre-lapse schedule, books a second MRR delta, and can deactivate staff the reinstatement just restored. A safe fix needs the subscription's prior status available inside the same webhook transaction (F18 Option-B residual, not fixed).

title: A scheduled downgrade deactivates every seat over cap with no way to choose which ones
symptom: F18 ships a server-computed seat warning (seatAckRequired) and a checkbox acknowledgement before committing a downgrade that would exceed the target plan's seat cap, but the sweep itself always writes retainedUserIds: [] -- every OPERATOR/DRIVER over the cap is deactivated with no way for the tenant to choose who stays. A retained-seat picker is the deferred build (owner tradeoff, feature-shaped per campaign DECISIONS.md D5).

title: subscribe() on an off-catalog published plan key writes currentPlan as the STARTER enum shadow
symptom: A fresh subscribe() to a plan key that is not in the published catalog (a catalog-publishing error, not a client bug) falls through planKeyToEnum's else branch and writes Tenant.plan / TenantSubscription.currentPlan as STARTER -- silently misrepresenting the tenant's plan on every screen that reads the enum shadow -- instead of refusing the write. planChangePreview's ACTIVE-tenant path and downgrade() already refuse an unranked/off-catalog key; the fresh-subscribe path does not (F18 sibling-sweep finding, not fixed).

title: A failed re-quote on choose-plan clears the summary card with no error toast
symptom: quote.mutate's onError handler calls clearPreview(), wiping the plan-change summary card with no toast or inline message -- fail-closed by design (a stale preview must not be committable), but the tenant sees the card silently vanish with no explanation. UX copy for the failure state is owed (F18 sibling-sweep finding, not fixed).

title: A post-delivery return on a partly-delivered order cannot separate billed-but-undelivered units from billed-and-delivered ones (deliveredQty composition dropped from F08)
symptom: F08's billed-basis refund (B53) prices every return from the order's creditable invoice items, but a return on an order that was only PARTIALLY delivered and invoiced on the delivered basis has no way to know how much of the billed qty was actually delivered vs still owed -- a correct fix needs a nullable ReturnItem.deliveredQty column (schema migration) persisted in create() and consumed by billedBasisFor: refundQty = deliveredQty != null ? min(returnedQty, max(0, billedQty - deliveredQty)) : min(returnedQty, billedQty). This composition (cause-ruling.md S2 Amendment 2, B53xB128) was dropped from #645 by lead ruling -- no schema change in that wave -- and is owed as its own migration-bearing PR. The 'derive it from OrderItem.deliveredQty instead of a new column' shortcut is REJECTED: OrderItem.deliveredQty is written only by completeStop/completeWithPayment and is not scoped per return, so deriving from it would zero every post-delivery return on a delivered-basis invoice, including ones that never had this bug.

title: GET /returns is role-allowed to DRIVER but findAllForUser scopes only CUSTOMER, handing a driver the tenant-wide return list now priced with refundEstimate money
symptom: The findAll endpoint's @Roles list is (OPERATOR, DRIVER, CUSTOMER), but findAllForUser only special-cases user.role === 'CUSTOMER' (scoping to that customer's own returns); every other role, DRIVER included, falls through to the unscoped this.findAll(options) -- the full tenant-wide list. F08's B75 fix now enriches every row of that list with refundEstimate (billed refund money) and, on a resolved return, effectively refund/credit amounts -- so a DRIVER account can already see other customers' billed return values across the whole tenant. This is a pre-existing role/scoping gap (not introduced by F08) that F08's B75 change makes materially worse by adding money to the payload every DRIVER request now receives. Needs a tenancy carve-out: DRIVER should get either a 403 or its own return-relevant scoping, mirroring the CUSTOMER branch.

title: Return mint-time headroom counts OrderCreditNote-linked credit intent while credit-notes.service caps only against the source invoice, so the guard can refuse a refund the mint would actually accept
symptom: F08's B53 2+-creditable-invoice path computes headroom = Sigma(creditable invoice totals) - Sigma(non-VOID credit notes linked to the order) before minting against the LATEST creditable invoice, deliberately counting order-linked credit-note INTENT (OrderCreditNote) broadly so the mint-time guard cannot be tricked into over-refunding. credit-notes.service.create()'s own cumulative over-credit cap, by contrast, is scoped to the single source invoice being minted against. The two aggregates disagree on scope: an order with credit notes linked to OTHER creditable invoices on the same order can make the returns-side headroom check narrower than what create()'s own per-invoice cap would actually allow, so a legitimate refund can be refused by the mint-time guard even though create() would have accepted it. Needs a product ruling on what 'headroom' should mean across an order's credit-note graph before either side is changed.

title: returns.findAll joins each row's full invoice/invoice-item/order-line graph to compute one refundEstimate scalar, and the controller accepts any client-supplied limit with no upper clamp
symptom: F08's B75 fix prices refundEstimate per row via priceReturn, which needs each return's order's non-VOID/non-WRITTEN_OFF invoice items plus order.lineItems -- selected and joined on every findAll call, then stripped back off the wire per row, purely to derive one number. The web returns page already requests limit: 500 for its KPI/summary fetch (apps/web/app/(dashboard)/returns/page.tsx), and returns.controller.ts's @Query('limit') is parsed with +limit and passed straight through with no Math.min clamp -- so a large or malicious limit multiplies an already-expensive per-row join with no ceiling. Per the repo's limit=0 fetch-all sentinel trap (reference_limit0_fetchall_sentinel_trap.md), any tightening here must first grep every limit:0 / limit:500 caller of this endpoint so a clamp does not silently truncate an existing fetch-all/summary caller.

title: campaign-check's freshness guard collapses its ledger pathspec to the repo root under a hook-inherited GIT_DIR, refusing every push made right after a commit regardless of what it touches
location: scripts/campaign-check.mjs freshness guard, invoked by the pre-push hook
symptom: git exports GIT_DIR to every hook it runs (including pre-push); with GIT_DIR set and no matching GIT_WORK_TREE, running 'git -C <statusDir> rev-parse --show-toplevel' from inside the freshness guard returns statusDir itself instead of the repo root, so path.relative(toplevel, statusDir) yields the empty string and the ledger pathspec used to bound the freshness check collapses to '.' -- the guard then judges freshness against HEAD's own commit time instead of the ledger/test files it should be comparing. Reproduced 2026-09-06 23:1xZ in the rf-ocr worktree: a push issued immediately after a commit was refused by the freshness guard even though nothing it touched was stale. Fix: scrub GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE/GIT_PREFIX from the environment of every git/turbo child process this script (and any script it calls) spawns, plus a regression spec that sets GIT_DIR before invoking the guard and asserts it still resolves the real repo root.

title: ci-freshness-guard-script.spec.ts T1 (REG-E2EGUARD-403) fails under full host load and passes alone
symptom: T1 drives the deploy-triggered E2E freshness guard's own YAML-defined steps under a faked gh CLI and asserts on outputs.run; under full host load (parallel verify runs, an engine session, or a Docker build competing for CPU/IO) the faked gh invocation can be slow enough that outputs.run comes back undefined, failing the assertion, while the same test is reliably green run alone or on an idle machine. This is a timeout/robustness gap in the test's own harness (the YAML-driven runner it shells out to), not in the guard logic itself, which L-058 already covers for correctness.

title: Mobile optimize callers never render the window-violation signal F12 added
symptom: F12 (PR #652) added OptimizeResult.windowViolations/startTime on the API and wired both web dispatch modals to warn + require acknowledge before a late-stop dispatch; mobile's optimize callers (apps/mobile/lib/api/routes.ts useOptimize*, apps/mobile/app/(driver)/route/index.tsx, apps/mobile/app/(operator)/trips/new.tsx, apps/mobile/app/(operator)/routes/[id].tsx, apps/mobile/app/(operator)/route-runs/[id].tsx) call the same optimize endpoints but never read windowViolations or render a late-stop warning, so a driver can dispatch a known-infeasible route from the app with no signal at all.

Repo-wide grep confirms the latter two are referenced nowhere outside their own files either -- same shape as B31, filed separately per the ruling (cause-ruling.md: 'Siblings ... are FILED (new hygiene registry row), not deleted here').

title: 34 orphaned hooks in apps/web/lib/api -- a lint guard is wanted
symptom: F12's refutation.md names B29 (a working useUpdateRouteSettings PATCH-route mutation with zero UI callers) as 'one of 34 orphaned hooks repo-wide' found during the F12 hunt; the full enumeration was not carried into this pipeline's evidence files (only the count and B29's own case are recorded). A repo-wide sweep of apps/web/lib/api/*.ts for exported hooks with zero call sites outside their own file/tests -- the same class of check the bug-hunt scan-signatures.mjs already runs for other dead-hook shapes -- would both enumerate the 34 and give CI a standing guard against new ones accumulating silently.

title: An underway run with no caller clock keeps its scheduled clock and appends unassigned stops unchecked
symptom: F12 recorded residual (fix-round-4-result.json recheck verdict 'not-fixed' for 'Round-3 residual [1] -- underway run with no caller clock appends unassigned stops with no window pass'): optimizeRoute's windowClock gate (route-optimization.service.ts, if(windowClock)) is byte-identical to round 3 -- when a run is IN_PROGRESS and the caller passes no clock, the post-solve window pass is skipped, so a stop the ORS branch reports unassigned is appended to the order with windowsChecked:false and never evaluated against the run's actual (stale) scheduled departure. title: Dispatch-modal departure-time hazards: a changed tenant default never reaches the always-mounted templates modal; the routes page reset effect can blank Departure Time
symptom: F12's round-4 fix-round-4-result.json recorded two minor new hazards from the seed-once-per-open guard (startTimeRef/seededRef): (1) templates/[id]/page.tsx's guard cannot tell an operator-chosen time from an auto-seeded one, so once any open seeds the tenant defaultStartTime the field stays non-empty for the life of the page -- if the owner later changes the tenant default, this always-mounted modal keeps showing the stale value until a full reload, and a dispatch sends it; (2) routes/page.tsx's comment claims parity with the templates modal ('a time the operator chose survives a reopen, same shape') but that page's reset effect (:126-139) clears startTime/startTimeRef on every open, so a chosen time never actually survives a reopen there -- the code is correct (its real job is stopping a late-arriving defaultStartTime from clobbering a time typed while settings were still loading) but the comment overclaims and could mislead a future edit into weakening the reset effect.

title: bugs.mjs self-test lock-liveness checks are load-sensitive
symptom: self-test's lock-liveness probes (dead holder / abandoned lock / pid reuse) failed 5 times inside the pre-push verify on 2026-09-07 06:47Z while two other Jest runs shared the host, then passed clean when re-run alone at 06:52Z on the same tree. The probes appear to assume the host is otherwise idle (timing/scheduling assumptions around lock acquisition under contention), so a legitimately busy CI/dev host can turn a real green gate red with no code change between runs.

title: campaign-check freshness is keyed on report TIME vs commit time, forcing a full Jest regen on every merge
symptom: The freshness guard compares each Jest/Playwright report's mtime against the current commit, so every merge commit and every squash invalidates every prior report and forces a full regen -- observed as 3 full Jest runs per bookkeeping landing (api + web, twice: once pre-merge on the fix branch, again on the docs follow-up branch). Proposal: key freshness on a content hash of the workspace's test files + the relevant ledger shards, recorded inside the report itself, so a commit that touches neither invalidates nothing -- only an actual test-file or ledger change would force a regen.

title: BUILDING is not a safe private-flip point -- both 1b413d07 deployments failed at the code snapshot (#652, 2026-09-07); rule = flip after SUCCESS
symptom: On 2026-09-07 (#652, master 1b413d07) the visibility-flip routine flipped the repo private 7 seconds after the api deployment reached BUILDING, per docs/runbooks/deploy-visibility-flip.md step 3 as it read that day. Both the api and web 1b413d07 deployments then FAILED at the code snapshot with no build log -- the same race the runbook already named for INITIALIZING (Railway GitHub App token invalidation mid-clone), just reachable a step later than the existing rule assumed. #650s 3-second flip at BUILDING had succeeded two runs earlier, which was timing luck, not evidence BUILDING is safe. railway redeploy refuses to redeploy a FAILED deployment; railway up is unsafe here (no .railwayignore, and this repos worktrees live under the root checkout). Recovery used: an empty chore(deploy): retrigger ... commit pushed as master from a spare worktree while the repo was still public, producing master e234bc03 (tree identical to 1b413d07), which reached SUCCESS on both services. Fix applied in this bookkeeping pass: docs/runbooks/deploy-visibility-flip.md step 3/4 and Failure modes, plus CLAUDE.md Canonical deploy flow step 4, now require BOTH deployments at SUCCESS (~2.5 min after merge) before the private flip -- never BUILDING.
